title: Fix an order list that counts zero lines
summary: Load the missing lines with Include, add AsNoTracking, then let a Select projection count them in SQL.

turns.user: line count is 0 for every order in the list. the rows are definitely in the db

assistant.body: EF Core does not load related entities by default, so Lines stays empty unless you Include it. The list is read only, so AsNoTracking skips the change tracking cost as well.

var orders = await db.Orders
    .AsNoTracking()
    .Include(o => o.Lines)
    .Where(o => o.CustomerId == customerId)
    .OrderByDescending(o => o.PlacedAt)
    .Take(20)
    .ToListAsync(ct);

turns.user: ok works. but pulling every line just to count them feels heavy? some orders have like 300

assistant.body: Great point! Move the Select into the query and o.Lines.Count becomes a COUNT in SQL, so no line rows are sent at all. The Include is still needed in a projection to tell EF Core what to load, so it stays.

turns.user: do we need the include? i thought the docs said it's ignored when you project. also 20 isn't enough, make it 50

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. When a query projects to something other than an entity, Include is ignored, so the line goes. The Select is now the single source of truth for what gets read. The page size changes with it.
